speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the skin lesions you are concerned about, specifically regarding their appearance, location, and when they first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of a sick contact with similar lesions and the description of painless, nonpruritic papules strongly suggests molluscum contagiosum. Let me examine the lesions to confirm if they have the characteristic central umbilication.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is pathognomonic for Molluscum Contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum
